docRequirement: `channels-reference.md` binds the delivery envelope, not just the transport. Line 244: "The event arrives in Claude's context wrapped in a `<channel>` tag. The `source` attribute is set automatically from your server's configured name:", followed by the literal rendering at :246-250 — `<channel source="your-channel" severity="high" run_id="1234">` with the `content` string as the tag body and `</channel>` closing it. The notification-format table adds the attribute rule (`:230`): `meta` is "Optional. Each entry becomes an attribute on the `<channel>` tag for routing context like chat ID, sender name, or alert severity. Keys must be identifiers: letters, digits, and underscores only. Keys containing hyphens or other characters are silently dropped." The two-way contract depends on that attribute channel existing: the `instructions` examples at :322, :350 and :620 read "Reply with the reply tool, passing the chat_id from the tag." So: one `<channel>` element per event, `source` = the server's configured name, one attribute per surviving `meta` key, non-identifier keys dropped, `content` as the body.
current: No `<channel>` element is ever built, and the attribute payload never enters the process. (1) Parse: `packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:357-361` — `this.client.setNotificationHandler(ClaudeChannelNotificationSchema, notification => { const text = (notification.params as { text?: unknown } | undefined)?.text; if (typeof text !== 'string' || !this.channelServer) return; this.channelHandler?.({ server: this.channelServer, text: boundedChannelText(text) }) })`. Only `params.text` is read; `params.meta` is never touched, so the per-key attributes are discarded at the transport seam. (2) Shape: `packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:102-105` — `export interface McpChannelMessage { server: string; text: string }`, no field for meta; the pool's guard `isMcpChannelMessage` (`packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:370-376`) validates only `server`/`text` and the 32 KiB bound (`MCP_CHANNEL_MAX_TEXT_BYTES`, `client.ts:173`, enforced by `boundedChannelText` at `:175-188`). (3) Fan-out keeps the slug: `packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:1082-1106` (`dispatchChannelMessage`) hands each subscriber the whole `{ server, text }`, and `subscribeChannel` (`mcp-pool.ts:714-722`) types listeners on that full message — nothing upstream has wrapped or stripped. (4) The consumer throws the identity away: `packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:2436-2439` — `managed.mcpChannelUnsubscribe = pool.subscribeChannel(leaserId, ({ text }) => { if (managed.mcpLeaserId !== leaserId) return; canDeliver()?.redirect(text) })`; `server` is destructured out of existence and the raw body is the whole payload. (5) Downstream nothing re-wraps: `PiAgent.redirect` (`packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:7109-7118`) sends `{ type: 'steer', message }`, `packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:4328-4333` calls `await piSession.steer(msg.message)` unchanged, and `ClaudeAgent.redirect` (`packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:2760-2769`) just assigns `this.pendingSteerMessage = message`. Absence control (`grep -a`, this repo has NUL-carrying files): `grep -rna '<channel' packages apps --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx'` returns only four unrelated CLI usage strings (`apps/cli/src/index.ts:918,940,2079,2080`). The positive control that the repo *can* do source-attributed wrapping is `packages/shared/src/prompts/guardian.ts:295-297` — `wrapUntrusted(label, body)` returns `` `<untrusted source="${label}">\n${neutralizeHarnessMarkers(body)}\n</untrusted>` `` — which is on the guardian prompt path only, never on the steer path. Adjacent: the server's `instructions` (the string the page says is "added to Claude's system prompt so it knows how to handle your events") are also never consumed — `grep -rna 'getInstructions' packages apps --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx'` → 0 hits.
divergence: The event body is right; the envelope is entirely missing. Three distinct deltas, in delivery order: (a) `meta` is never parsed, so the attribute payload the page specifies at `:230` does not exist anywhere in the process (`client.ts:358` reads `params.text` only) and `McpChannelMessage` has no field to carry it (`client.ts:102-105`); (b) the source slug IS carried to the seam intact but is dropped by the subscriber's destructure `({ text })` at `SessionManager.ts:2436`; (c) nothing anywhere composes the `<channel …>…</channel>` element, so the model receives the bare body as an ordinary mid-turn steer — indistinguishable from user-typed text, with no `source` and no `chat_id`-style routing key. This is not a key-name mismatch and not a value bug: the tag itself does not exist. (The `content` vs `text` param name and the missing `notifications/` method prefix are f135's delta, in the same handler; f134 owns idle queueing/grouping; f137 owns the permission relay.)

change.what: Add `meta?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>` to `McpChannelMessage`. In the handler, after reading the body (f135 renames that read to `params.content`, keeping `params.text` as a fallback), parse `params.meta`: accept only own enumerable entries whose key matches `/^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$/` and whose value is a `string`, and SILENTLY drop the rest — `:230` says hyphenated/other keys "are silently dropped", so no warning and no rejection of the event. Bound it like the body is bounded (cap the entry count and per-value length next to `MCP_CHANNEL_MAX_TEXT_BYTES` at `:173`) and run each value through the same `INVALID_CHANNEL_CONTROL` strip `boundedChannelText` uses (`:172-188`), plus strip/escape `"`, `<`, `>` and newlines so a hostile value cannot terminate the attribute or the tag. Drop a `source` key if a server sends one — `source` is ours to set. Keep `server: this.channelServer` as the source value (the pool's slug, set at `mcp-pool.ts:1138`); if the doc's "server's configured name" must mean the handshake name instead, `getServerInfo()` at `:466-471` already exposes it — decide once and comment which.

Extend the guard so `meta`, when present, is a plain object whose every value is a string and every key matches the identifier rule — the guard is the fail-closed boundary between an untrusted server and the prompt, and it must not let an unsanitized record through even if `client.ts` is bypassed (tests inject `PoolClient`s directly: `packages/server-core/src/sessions/__tests__/mcp-channel-gate.test.ts:10-19`). `dispatchChannelMessage` (:1082-1106) needs no change — it already forwards the whole message — and `subscribeChannel` (:714-722) needs none either, since its listener type is `(message: McpChannelMessage) => void`.

One renderer, so every consumer emits the same envelope: `<channel source="<server>"` + ` k="v"` per surviving meta entry in insertion order + `>\n` + body + `\n</channel>`. Defang the body with `neutralizeHarnessMarkers` from `packages/shared/src/prompts/untrusted-text.ts` (the precedent is `wrapUntrusted` at `packages/shared/src/prompts/guardian.ts:295-297`) so a literal `</channel>` inside an event cannot close the fence and forge trusted structure after it. Export from the package's `mcp` entry (`packages/shared/src/mcp/index.ts`, which already exports `McpChannelMessage`).

Effectively one line: stop destructuring `({ text })`, take the whole message, and deliver `canDeliver()?.redirect(formatChannelEvent(message))`. Leave the leaser guard at `:2437` and `canDeliver()` (:2399-2405) exactly as they are. Do NOT touch the sibling plugin-monitor delivery at `:2418-2421` — that is the `plugins-reference.md` monitor contract, not a channel, and wrapping it would be a different (undocumented) envelope.

blastRadius: Same-process only — no wire or persistence schema changes shape. The steer IPC already carries an opaque string (`packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:7116` `this.send({ type: 'steer', message })` → `packages/pi-agent-server/src/index.ts:4331` `piSession.steer(msg.message)`), and `ClaudeAgent.redirect` (`packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:2767`) only stores it, so a longer string needs no protocol edit. What it DOES cross: the delivered string becomes part of the session's conversation history in the Pi subprocess, so stored transcripts of channel-bearing sessions change content (not shape) from that release on — old sessions keep the unwrapped form. Readers to update or re-verify: `packages/server-core/src/sessions/__tests__/mcp-channel-gate.test.ts` (:77, :87, :99, :105 all assert raw text); `packages/shared/tests/mcp-pool.test.ts:703-790` (channel fan-out, drain and leaser-scoping tests built on `McpChannelMessage`); `packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.process-supervisor.test.ts:981` (stub `subscribeChannel` typed `(event: { server: string; text: string })` — widening the interface touches this signature) and `:1022`, `:1055` (unsubscribe ordering). Interface consumers of the widened type: `PoolClient.setChannelHandler` (`packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:246`), `NessyMcpClient.channelHandler` (:279) and `setChannelHandler` (:671), `channelSubscribers` (`mcp-pool.ts:630`). The gate itself is untouched: `ChannelPolicy`/`allowedSources`/`deniedSources` (`mcp-pool.ts:341-361`), `CHANNEL_PUSH_OFF`, `setChannelPolicy` (:731-736) and `SessionManager.resolveChannelPolicy` (:2552) all keep their meaning. Imported-plugin path: any plugin-bundled MCP server declaring `capabilities.experimental['claude/channel']` starts receiving the documented envelope, which is what its `instructions` already describe — but those `instructions` are still never injected (`getInstructions` → 0 hits), so that half stays broken and belongs to its own finding.
userImpact: Observable today, on the two-way path. With `channelsEnabled` on and a channel source pushing during a live turn, the event body is injected as if the user had typed it mid-turn: no source, no attributes. A user running a chat-bridge channel (the page's own webhook example) sees the model unable to route a reply — the `chat_id` it is told to pass back never appears in its context, so it either omits the argument, invents one, or asks the user which conversation this was; with two channel sources armed on one session the model cannot say which one fired, and can attribute an alert to the wrong system. For a one-way alert channel the effect is milder but still visible: the alert reads as a user instruction, so the model tends to act on it as a new task rather than as an event to note. Latent half: nothing surfaces at all while a session is idle, because that push is dropped before this code runs (f134).
